### fixture 0
KG-007
  Medium
  PodSecurity
  Deployment/legacy:api
  container "api" has a writable root filesystem, letting an attacker drop tooling or modify binaries inside the running container
  Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem to true and mount an emptyDir over any directory the process must write to, such as /tmp.
  kubectl patch deployment legacy -n demo --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext/readOnlyRootFilesystem","value":true}]'
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/
---
KG-007
  Medium
  PodSecurity
  Deployment/legacy:sidecar
  container "sidecar" has a writable root filesystem, letting an attacker drop tooling or modify binaries inside the running container
  Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem to true and mount an emptyDir over any directory the process must write to, such as /tmp.
  kubectl patch deployment legacy -n demo --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/1/securityContext/readOnlyRootFilesystem","value":true}]'
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/
---
KG-010
  High
  Network
  Namespace/demo
  namespace "demo" has no default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy, so every pod in the cluster can reach every pod here
  Apply a default-deny ingress policy, then add explicit allow policies for the traffic each workload actually serves.
  apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-ingress
  namespace: demo
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/
---
KG-011
  High
  Governance
  Namespace/demo
  namespace "demo" does not set pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce, so Pod Security Admission enforces nothing and any pod spec is accepted
  Label the namespace with a Pod Security Standard. Start at baseline to catch the worst cases, then move to restricted once workloads comply.
  kubectl label namespace demo pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-admission/
---
KG-012
  Medium
  RBAC
  ServiceAccount/default
  the default ServiceAccount automounts an API token into 1 workload(s) (Deployment/legacy) that do not appear to need API access
  Disable automounting on the default ServiceAccount, and give workloads that do call the API their own ServiceAccount with a scoped Role.
  kubectl patch serviceaccount default -n demo -p '{"automountServiceAccountToken":false}'
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/
---
KG-013
  High
  RBAC
  Role/legacy
  Role "legacy" grants a wildcard on apiGroups, resources and verbs, which silently expands as new resources and verbs are added to the cluster
  Replace each wildcard with the explicit apiGroups, resources and verbs the subject needs. Use kubectl auth can-i --list to confirm nothing breaks.
  kubectl get role legacy -n demo -o yaml
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/
---
KG-020
  Medium
  SupplyChain
  Deployment/legacy:api
  container "api" uses image "nginx" with no tag, which resolves to latest and can change between restarts
  Pin the image to an immutable tag, or better a digest, so every replica runs the artifact you tested.
  kubectl set image Deployment/legacy api=nginx@sha256:<digest> -n demo
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/#image-names
---
KG-020
  Medium
  SupplyChain
  Deployment/legacy:sidecar
  container "sidecar" uses the mutable tag latest, so the running image can drift from the reviewed one without any manifest change
  Pin the image to a release tag or a digest, so rollouts are reproducible and auditable.
  kubectl set image Deployment/legacy sidecar=registry.example.com:5000/proxy:latest@sha256:<digest> -n demo
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/#image-names
---
KG-021
  Medium
  Governance
  Deployment/legacy:api
  container "api" is missing memory limit, cpu request and memory request, so it can starve neighbours on the node and makes the namespace a denial-of-service vector
  Set both requests and limits. Requests drive scheduling and limits cap the blast radius of a runaway process.
  kubectl patch deployment legacy -n demo --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources","value":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"128Mi"},"limits":{"memory":"512Mi"}}}]'
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/
---
KG-021
  Medium
  Governance
  Deployment/legacy:sidecar
  container "sidecar" is missing memory limit, cpu request and memory request, so it can starve neighbours on the node and makes the namespace a denial-of-service vector
  Set both requests and limits. Requests drive scheduling and limits cap the blast radius of a runaway process.
  kubectl patch deployment legacy -n demo --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/1/resources","value":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"128Mi"},"limits":{"memory":"512Mi"}}}]'
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/
---
### fixture 1
### fixture 2
KG-011
  High
  Governance
  Namespace/demo
  namespace "demo" enforces the privileged Pod Security Standard, which applies no restrictions at all
  Raise enforcement to baseline or restricted. privileged is only appropriate for namespaces running node-level infrastructure.
  kubectl label --overwrite namespace demo pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-admission/
---
